current_answer: A Swedish test of an AI-project grant found more job ads, not a detected headcount boom or collapse. Among firms that applied for first-time AI-project funding, recipients were 24 percentage points more likely to post a vacancy five years later, especially in white-collar work, but the study did not detect a total-employment, hiring or separation effect. That is a causal estimate of a Swedish grant among applicant firms—not proof that generative AI raises jobs everywhere. U.S. early-career exposure studies and a Danish reported-adoption study still show narrower, contested hiring warnings, while the 4% 2030 figure remains a model scenario, not jobs already lost.

catalogue_card.question: Did a real AI rollout cut jobs in Sweden?
catalogue_card.text: The closest causal test here found the opposite of a simple layoff story: an AI-project grant increased vacancy posting, while the study detected no change in headcount, hiring or separations.

summary: A Swedish grant for first-time AI projects made recipient firms more likely to post vacancies, especially white-collar vacancies, five years later.
The study did not detect a change in total employment, hiring or separations. More job ads are not proof of more completed hires or jobs.
The result is a Swedish grant effect among applicant firms, mostly before widespread generative-AI chatbot use. It does not settle the separate U.S. early-career or Danish hiring signals.
A 4% 2030 cognitive-employment figure remains one model scenario, not a current job-loss count.
uncertainty: The intervention was a grant for first-time AI projects, not randomized use of one named system or generative AI.
The sample is 190 Swedish applicant firms. Synthetic difference-in-differences improves the comparison but cannot make every changing difference disappear.
Vacancies measure attempted recruitment. The paper did not find a statistically detectable effect on its register measures of total employment, hiring or separations.
No current study can predict a reader’s own job loss or prescribe a career decision.
freshness_note: Checked 21 September 2026. A newly added quasi-experimental Swedish grant study changes the evidence map: AI-project support increased vacancy posting without a detected headcount, hiring or separation effect.
